tighten security: After the break-in last month, the school decided to tighten security by installing cameras at every gate.
上個月發生闖入事件後，學校決定在每個校門裝設攝影機來加強安檢。
tighten one's belt: Since my father lost his job, our whole family has had to tighten our belts and stop eating out.
自從我爸爸失業後，我們全家不得不勒緊褲帶，不再外出用餐。
tighten the rules: The principal said the old phone policy was too loose, so he decided to tighten the rules this semester.
校長說舊的手機規定太寬鬆，所以他決定這學期收緊規定。
tighten one's grip: As the wind grew stronger, I had to tighten my grip on the umbrella so it wouldn't blow away.
風變得越來越強，我必須握緊雨傘，免得它被吹走。
tighten controls: The government plans to tighten controls on imported meat to stop the disease from spreading into Taiwan.
政府計畫加強管制進口肉品，以阻止疾病傳入台灣。
tighten a screw: The chair kept shaking, so my dad used a screwdriver to tighten a screw under the seat.
椅子一直晃動，所以我爸爸用螺絲起子鎖緊座位下的一顆螺絲。
tilt the balance: The new player's amazing speed could tilt the balance in our favor during tomorrow's final game.
新球員驚人的速度可能在明天的決賽中打破平衡，讓局勢對我們有利。
tilt in favor of: As more evidence appeared in the news, public opinion began to tilt in favor of the young driver.
隨著新聞中出現越來越多證據，輿論開始傾向於那位年輕駕駛。
tilt one's head: The puppy would tilt its head to one side whenever it heard a strange sound outside.
每當聽到外面有奇怪的聲音，那隻小狗就會把頭歪向一邊。
tilt the scales: Her excellent interview helped tilt the scales, and she got the job over two other strong candidates.
她出色的面試表現幫忙改變了局勢，讓她在另外兩位優秀人選中脫穎而出得到工作。
tilt toward: Many young voters' opinions began to tilt toward the candidate who promised cheaper housing.
許多年輕選民的意見開始傾向那位承諾讓房價更便宜的候選人。
time one's arrival: We tried to time our arrival so that we would reach the station just before the last train left.
我們試著安排抵達時間，好在末班車開走前剛好到達車站。
well-timed: Her well-timed phone call came just as I was about to give up and leave the office.
她那通時機恰當的電話正好在我準備放棄、離開辦公室時打來。
time a race: The coach used a stopwatch to time a race between the two fastest runners in our class.
教練用碼錶為我們班上兩位跑最快的同學的比賽計時。
badly timed: His badly timed visit came right in the middle of dinner, so we all had to stop eating to greet him.
他時機不對的來訪正好在晚餐中途，所以我們全都得停下來去招呼他。
time the market: Experts warn that it is almost impossible to time the market and always buy stocks at their lowest price.
專家警告，要抓市場時機、總是在最低價買進股票幾乎是不可能的。
tip the balance: In the end, a lower price may tip the balance, and we might buy the smaller apartment near the station.
最後，較低的價格可能會打破平衡，我們或許會買下車站附近那間較小的公寓。
tip the scales: Her years of volunteer work may tip the scales when the university chooses between two strong applicants.
當大學在兩位優秀申請者之間做選擇時，她多年的志工經歷可能會起決定作用。
tip someone off: A neighbor called to tip the police off about the stolen bikes hidden in the old warehouse.
一位鄰居打電話向警方通風報信，說有贓車藏在那間舊倉庫裡。
tip over: Be careful not to tip over the cup, or the hot coffee will spill all over your laptop.
小心別把杯子翻倒，否則熱咖啡會灑滿你的筆電。
tip the waiter: In Taiwan most people don't tip the waiter, because a service charge is usually added to the bill.
在台灣大多數人不會給服務生小費，因為帳單通常已加了服務費。
tip of the iceberg: The few complaints we received are just the tip of the iceberg; many more customers are probably unhappy.
我們收到的少數投訴只是冰山一角，可能還有更多顧客感到不滿。
tire of the game: Children usually tire of the game after a few days and then ask their parents for a new one.
孩子們通常幾天後就對遊戲厭倦，然後向父母要新的遊戲。
never tire of saying: My grandmother never tires of saying that hard work is the key to success in life.
我奶奶總是不厭其煩地說，努力是人生成功的關鍵。
tire someone out: The long hike up the mountain tired the kids out, so they fell asleep right after dinner.
長途登山讓孩子們筋疲力盡，所以他們一吃完晚餐就睡著了。
tired of waiting: After standing in line for two hours, many fans got tired of waiting and went home.
排隊站了兩個小時後，許多粉絲等得不耐煩就回家了。
toast the winner: At the end of the dinner, everyone raised their glasses to toast the winner of the speech contest.
晚宴結束時，大家舉起酒杯為演講比賽的獲勝者舉杯慶祝。
propose a toast: At my sister's wedding, my father stood up to propose a toast to the happy couple.
在我姊姊的婚禮上，我爸爸站起來向這對新人敬酒。
the toast of the town: After winning the national singing contest, the shy teenager suddenly became the toast of the town.
贏得全國歌唱比賽後，那位害羞的青少年突然成了全城追捧的人物。
toast bread: Every morning my mom likes to toast bread and spread some butter and jam on it for us.
每天早上我媽媽喜歡烤麵包，並為我們抹上一些奶油和果醬。
be toast: If the teacher finds out that I copied my friend's homework, I'm going to be toast.
如果老師發現我抄朋友的作業，我就完蛋了。
